name: Beveled '95 Desktop
summary: Mid-90s desktop nostalgia: cascading spreadsheet windows, a Pulse alert dialog and a Start button that says Start free.
look: Acme-teal desktop, grey 4-tone bevelled windows with teal gradient title bars, white wells, pixel-crisp dialogs and a taskbar with tray clock. Chunky Manrope UI type, one serif italic word in text files.

components.name: Bevelled window
components.role: grey #C6C6C6 frame with 4-tone inset bevel and teal gradient title bar

components.name: Cascade stack
components.role: dashboard_33…38.xls windows offset 34 px — the dashboard pile

components.name: Modal dialog
components.role: warning / alert box with icon, message and a focused default button

components.name: Splash screen
components.role: bevelled panel with the Acme mark and version line

components.name: Taskbar & tray
components.role: clock and tray icon; the tray hosts Pulse in the background

components.name: Start menu
components.role: vertical brand band + coloured items; the Start button reads Start free

motion.name: Cascade spawn
motion.how: each window appears instantly (no easing) with a 2-frame outline zoom, one per 8th note — authentic and rhythmic

motion.name: Minimise-all
motion.how: windows scale 1→0 toward their taskbar slots, power2.in 0.25 s, all on the drop

motion.name: Cursor glide & click
motion.how: cursor moves along a slight arc, power1.inOut 0.75 s, button bevel inverts for 2 frames exactly on the beat

story: Hook: six cascading dashboard_XX.xls windows, notes.txt asking "How many dashboards did you check today?" and a warning dialog "The drop still shipped on Friday." Reveal: everything minimises; an Acme Pulse splash screen appears. Proof: a live metrics window drops coral after the deploy line and the Pulse dialog reports checkout conversion −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231 with Roll back (default) / Acknowledge; the cursor clicks Roll back. CTA: readme.txt "You ship. Pulse watches.", a start menu of benefits and a Start free button.
adapt: Rebuild your real UI screenshots inside bevelled windows, cast your product's key notification as the modal dialog, and relabel the Start button with your CTA.

references.note: mid-90s desktop UI conventions: taskbar, Start button, bevelled 3D widgets
Susan Kare: pixel icons and early GUI visual language

fit.risk: Dated or parody feel; must avoid real OS logos, sounds and trademarks.

best_for: B2B with a sense of humour
